headline: Hormuz oil shock, Alberta's vote and Toronto's tight race shaped the week
summary: Hormuz tanker attacks kept Brent near $110 (touching $111.99), feeding 3.7% U.S. and 3.1% Canadian inflation. Albertans rejected separation by roughly 75% to 25% (unofficial) as Toronto's mayoral race tightened ahead of October 26.

top.headline: Brent near $110 as Hormuz tanker attacks continue
top.what: Brent touched $111.99 on Tuesday before settling at $108.79 and hovering near $110 Wednesday as tanker attacks and mine reports continued; Iran's conditional reopening plan is unaccepted.
top.why: It is the main reason gas, diesel and grocery prices stay high in Ontario.

top.headline: Canada's inflation edges up to 3.1% on gasoline
top.what: Gasoline up 27.8% pushed headline inflation to 3.1%, while core measures eased to about 1.9%.
top.why: It shapes the Bank of Canada's October 28 decision and what Ontarians pay at the pump.

top.headline: U.S. inflation jumps to 3.7%
top.what: Record gas prices pushed U.S. consumer prices up 3.7% from a year earlier, and traders now see close to even odds of a Federal Reserve hike on October 28.
top.why: Higher U.S. rates and bond yields can push up Canadian mortgage rates.

top.headline: Alberta votes about 75% to stay in Canada in separation referendum
top.what: Albertans voted roughly 75–77% to remain in Canada (unofficial); Smith pledged no second referendum while she is premier.
top.why: It settles, for now, a national unity question that had shadowed trade talks and investment.

top.headline: Trade war with the U.S. shows no thaw
top.what: Trump said Canada will end up the 51st state, his ambassador warned Canadian politicians off the midterms, and Poilievre toured Michigan to push for tariff-free auto trade.
top.why: Ontario's auto and steel jobs are the most exposed in the country.

top.headline: U.S. early voting surges as Democrats lead midterm polls
top.what: Georgia set an early-voting record, an AP-NORC poll found about half of voters want Democrats in control of Congress, and the Justice Department sued California over mail ballots.
top.why: Control of Congress after November 3 decides how freely Trump can act on tariffs that hit Ontario industries.

top.headline: Russia pounds Ukraine's grid as Kyiv–Washington rift widens
top.what: Massive strikes on power plants left hundreds of thousands without electricity, Ukraine dropped Trump's energy truce, and EU leaders pledged continued support in Brussels.
top.why: Refinery strikes and a U.S.-Ukraine split affect world diesel supply and NATO allies, including Canada.

top.headline: Stelco layoffs begin in Hamilton
top.what: Cleveland-Cliffs is pressing ahead with up to 500 Hamilton layoffs despite a five-business-day federal deadline, and Ottawa says it could seek a court-ordered sale.
top.why: It is the clearest local sign of how the trade war is hitting Ontario industry.
